blocks.prompt: 1. Find the linear approximation of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x + 1}\) at \(x = 3\), and use it to approximate \(\sqrt{3.1}\) and \(\sqrt{2.9}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh linearization ka sawal hai: pehle \(\sqrt{x + 1}\) ki \(x = 3\) par tangent line banani hai, phir use andaze ke liye use karna hai.
Diya kya hai? Function aur centre \(x = 3\). Find kya karna hai? \(L(x)\), aur \(\sqrt{3.1}\), \(\sqrt{2.9}\) ke andaze.
Ghaur karein: \(\sqrt{3.1}\) tab banega jab \(x + 1 = 3.1\), yani \(x = 2.1\); aur \(\sqrt{2.9}\) ke liye \(x = 1.9\).
Plan: \(f(3)\), \(f'(3)\), \(L(x)\), phir dono \(x\) values rakh kar andaza, aur calculator se muqabla.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x + 1}\), centre \(a = 3\).
Maloom karna: \(L(x)\), aur \(\sqrt{3.1}\), \(\sqrt{2.9}\) ke andaze.
Tareeqa: \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\). \(a = 3\) par \(x + 1 = 4\) perfect square hai, is liye values bilkul exact niklengi.

Centre par value
\[f(3) = \sqrt{3 + 1} = \sqrt{4} = 2\]
Kyun: tangent line point \((3, 2)\) se guzregi; yeh hamara shuruaati point hai.

Centre par derivative
\[f'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}(x + 1)^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}\]
\[f'(3) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{1}{4}\]
Kyun: square root ko power \(\frac{1}{2}\) likh kar power rule lagaya; chain rule mein andar ka derivative \((x + 1)' = 1\) hai, is liye koi extra factor nahi aaya.

Linearization
\[L(x) = 2 + \tfrac{1}{4}(x - 3)\]
\[= \dfrac{x + 5}{4}\]
Yani \(x = 3\) ke qareeb \(\sqrt{x + 1} \approx \dfrac{x + 5}{4}\).
Kyun: 2 ko \(\frac{8}{4}\) likha, phir \(8 + x - 3 = x + 5\). Ab square root ki jagah ek seedhi line hai.

\(\sqrt{3.1}\) ka andaza: yahan \(x + 1 = 3.1\), to \(x = 2.1\)
\[\sqrt{3.1} \approx \dfrac{2.1 + 5}{4} = \dfrac{7.1}{4}\]
\[= 1.775\]
Calculator: \(\sqrt{3.1} = 1.76068\); ghalti takreeban \(0.0143\).
Kyun: \(\sqrt{3.1}\) asal mein \(f(2.1)\) hai, is liye \(L\) mein 2.1 rakha.
Dhyan dein: \(x = 3.1\) rakh dena aam ghalti hai; woh \(\sqrt{4.1}\) dega, \(\sqrt{3.1}\) nahi.

\(\sqrt{2.9}\) ka andaza: yahan \(x + 1 = 2.9\), to \(x = 1.9\)
\[\sqrt{2.9} \approx \dfrac{1.9 + 5}{4} = \dfrac{6.9}{4}\]
\[= 1.725\]
Calculator: \(\sqrt{2.9} = 1.70294\); ghalti takreeban \(0.0221\).
Kyun: bilkul wahi tareeqa, bas \(x = 1.9\).

Tasdeeq
2.1 aur 1.9 centre 3 se takreeban ek unit door hain, is liye ghaltiyan (0.014 aur 0.022) Example 22 se zyada hain. Dono andaze thore bare hain, kyun ke \(\sqrt{x + 1}\) ka graph neeche murta hai aur tangent line us ke upar rehti hai. 1.9 zyada door hai, is liye us ki ghalti bhi zyada hai.

blocks.text: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x + 1}\) ka centre \(x = 3\) ho to \(\sqrt{3.1}\) aur \(\sqrt{2.9}\) asal mein \(f(2.1)\) aur \(f(1.9)\) hain, jo centre se kaafi door hain. Lagta hai sawal \(f(3.1) = \sqrt{4.1}\) aur \(f(2.9) = \sqrt{3.9}\) poochna chahta tha. Us surat mein: \(\sqrt{4.1} \approx \frac{3.1 + 5}{4} = 2.025\) (calculator 2.02485) aur \(\sqrt{3.9} \approx \frac{2.9 + 5}{4} = 1.975\) (calculator 1.97484), aur ghalti bohat kam hai. Upar humne sawal waise hi hal kiya jaise chhapa hai.
